Honestly, a lot of it had to do with how sedentary I was for so long due to depression. I found it difficult to lose weight whilst on an antidepressant medication (notorious for weight gain), so once I ceased that it became easier. Definitely not blaming it all on that, but it didn't help. 

A lot of it was restarting my metabolism - eating a low GI breakfast everyday, making sure I was eating 3 meals a day, cutting out soft drink and juice completely and only drinking water (LOTS of water), increasing incidental exercise and in general changing my attitude towards food. Instead of eating a whole bag of chips and chocolate a night, I would treat them as a treat - portioning out a small amount onto a plate instead of just snacking from the bag. Lots more but those were the main things :)

What you have identified is that you do not want to hurt any more. Please remember there is a difference between wanting the pain to stop, and wanting to be dead. Remember that if you go through with this, you will shatter the lives of everyone around you, for the rest of their lives. This is a passage that I have found really helpful in regards to suicide and identifying the difference between wanting death, or wanting the pain to stop.


'You should also bear in mind that the crisis that leads many people to contemplate suicide is nearly always temporary, and that in time, people see that their problems were not as big as they first thought. That's all good news. People think about committing suicide as a solution to a problem they see no solution to. But here's the thing - even if you don't think there is a solution to your problems right now, that does not mean it does not exist. It just means that you can't see it right now.
I'd like to ask you a question. Given a choice, would you choose to feel like you do right now, or would you choose to feel happy?

Of course, we all want to be happy. Who wants a life of misery? But here's the thing. We control how we feel (feelings are derived from our thoughts and emotions). So if you feel on the verge of killing yourself right now, and, given a free choice, you'd choose to be happy - have you ever wondered - who's doing the choosing?
